entries.title: DRAFT: a bounded-degree nontransitive tree can percolate at criticality
entries.statement: DRAFT, author-written and not independently reviewed. Let T be the rooted tree where every generation k-1 vertex has 8 children if k is a power of 2 and 2 children otherwise, k>=1. For independent Bernoulli bond percolation on T, the maximum degree is 9, p_c(T)=1/2 and theta_T(1/2)>=4/5. Writing Z_n for root-connected generation-n vertices, E[Z_n]=(2p)^n 4^(1+floor(log_2 n)), and at p=1/2 the normalized second moment is at most 5/4. This explicitly refutes a general critical-nonpercolation inference based only on independence, finite energy, bounded degree and finite-event continuity. T is not quasi-transitive and this is not a counterexample to the Z^d conjecture.

source.excerpt: The counterexample is a nontransitive tree, not Z^d.

entries.title: DRAFT: a shrinking subcritical window can preserve finite-generation survival
entries.statement: DRAFT, author-written and not independently reviewed. For the explicit dyadic-branching tree with 8 children at power-of-two generations and 2 otherwise, let f_n(p)=P_p(Z_n>0). For 0<p_n=1/2-delta_n<1/2, f_n(p_n)>=4/5-delta_n n/p_n. Indeed open pivotal edges lie on any root-to-level-n path, so their number is at most n and finite-product differentiation gives f_n_prime(p)<=n/p. Therefore delta_n n->0 cannot also make f_n(p_n)->0. Finite-volume continuity and subcritical vanishing at each fixed parameter do not license exchanging these limits.

source.excerpt: The counterexample is a nontransitive tree, not Z^d.

entries.title: DRAFT: the fixed backward interval is the open proof obligation
entries.statement: DRAFT audit concept, not a proof of critical nonpercolation. For independent nearest-neighbour Bernoulli bonds on Z^d, define A_n as origin-to-boundary connection inside [-n,n]^d, f_n(p)=P_p(A_n), and lambda_n(p) as the conditional expected number of open pivotal edges given A_n. For 0<a<b<1, log(f_n(b)/f_n(a))=integral_a^b lambda_n(s)/s ds. Under a hypothetical theta(p_c)>0, ruling out a critical jump via this identity requires a finite liminf of that integral on one fixed [a,p_c] with a<p_c, or another rigorously derived geometric mechanism. Endpoint bounds and intervals shrinking with n do not establish this premise. w423 states the premise explicitly and has not proved it for the lattice.
assumptions: The claimed lattice estimate is unproved

source.excerpt: A bound at p_c alone, or a different a_n for every n, does not suffice.

relations.rationale: The narrow-window survival lower bound uses the explicit tree and its critical 4/5 lower bound.
The tree exhibits failure of exchanging parameter and scale limits; the lattice criterion requires a fixed interval. This is an analogy, not a proof transfer.
The bounded-degree nontransitive counterexample tests unrestricted inferences used when approaching C0023; it neither refutes nor proves the Z^d claim.
The exact missing fixed-interval premise concerns attempts to prove the C0023 critical bond statement; its validity on Z^d remains open in this packet.
